title: Derivative of the moment gap
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $p,q,\rho,t\in\mathbb R$, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Suppose that $1+tX(x)>0$ and $1+\rho tX(x)>0$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Then the hypercontractive moment gap is differentiable at $t$, with derivative equal to the difference between $q$ times the derivative of the first affine moment raised to the power $q$, and $p$ times the derivative of the second affine moment raised to the power $p$, as specified by the moment-gap derivative.
